target.title: fix(discord): bound stalled probe response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord probe checks could hang after the `getMe` request returned response headers but the JSON response body stopped producing data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord probe now reads the successful `getMe` JSON body through the bounded response reader with the existing 16 MiB cap and a per-chunk timeout tied to the probe timeout. Application metadata reads are also bounded, and the status entry point carries only the remaining caller timeout through cold lazy loading. Existing non-OK handling, malformed JSON wording, and the already-resolved bot result are preserved.

## User Impact

Discord configuration checks now return from stalled response bodies instead of waiting indefinitely. If optional application metadata stalls, the successful bot identity remains available.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/probe.intents.test.ts extensions/discord/src/channel.test.ts extensions/discord/src/api.test.ts` (`3` files, `63` tests passed)
- `git diff --check b0ebb81e89f5217397d409c996e2bbf914623a94..HEAD`
- Claude autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings

## Proof

### Exact-current-head controlled local HTTP production-path proof

Exact head: `3a470fcd81a815982a1669c4568518bb75551331`.

Command:

```text
git rev-parse HEAD
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY -u http_proxy -u https_proxy -u all_proxy timeout 30s ./node_modules/.bin/tsx --no-cache scratchpad/discord-probe-current-head-proof.ts
```

The temporary harness called the production `discordPlugin.status.probeAccount()` and `probeDiscord()` paths. It used a real loopback `node:http` server and real Node `fetch`; the existing fetch seam only rewrote the fixed Discord origin to loopback while forwarding the production request options and abort signal. No mocked `Response`, Discord traffic, or credentials were used.

Redacted transcript:

```text
3a470fcd81a815982a1669c4568518bb75551331
proof=controlled-local-http production-path=discord-status+probe
cold-status-app-stall ok=true bot=proof-bot application=undefined elapsed=290ms callerBudget=300ms socketAborted=true
normal ok=true bot=proof-bot application=app-proof elapsed=7ms
get-me-stall ok=false error="discord.probe.getMe: JSON response stalled after 140ms" elapsed=188ms socketAborted=true
recovery-after-get-me-stall ok=true bot=proof-bot application=app-proof elapsed=6ms
application-stall ok=true bot=proof-bot application=undefined elapsed=200ms callerBudget=220ms socketAborted=true
final-recovery ok=true bot=proof-bot application=app-proof elapsed=6ms
requests=11 assertions=passed
```

Observed:

- The first status probe in the process cold-loaded the lazy probe runtime. A partial application-metadata body then stalled, was aborted, and returned in `290ms` within the `300ms` caller budget; the resolved bot identity remained present and optional application metadata was omitted.
- A partial `getMe` JSON body that stopped producing bytes returned the production idle-timeout error and closed the server response before `writableEnded` (`socketAborted=true`).
- A direct stalled application-metadata response also closed before `writableEnded`, returned inside the `220ms` caller budget, and preserved `ok=true` plus the bot identity.
- Normal probes before and after the failures returned both bot and application data, demonstrating later-call recovery. All harness assertions passed with exit `0`.

Known limits: this is controlled local real-HTTP production-path proof, not live Discord. It does not claim live Discord behavior or credentialed testing. The `getMe` body protection is an idle/per-chunk timeout, not a total response deadline, so this proof covers a body that stops producing data and does not claim protection from an indefinitely slow trickle. The temporary uncommitted harness was removed after the run.


This exact-head section supersedes the earlier `f6de53aba381701e59a0554a8ffe80c9c5b76457` transcript.
